verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev exposes a documented Management API (with API-key or personal-access-token auth) that covers core operations UI users perform — triggering/canceling/retrying runs, deploying projects, monitoring runs, and multi-project/environment management (docs-23, docs-24, docs-27, docs-33) — and this API is also what its official MCP server wraps for AI assistants (docs-18, docs-29, probe-4). However, probes show no discoverable OpenAPI/swagger spec (probe-3) or docs.md (probe-2), and there's no evidence that UI-only features like TRQL querying (docs-10) or full observability dashboards are exposed via API, and a user reported friction triggering tasks from the frontend requiring a proxy (comm-15). Missing for 10: a published OpenAPI/API reference confirming full endpoint parity, API access to TRQL/observability querying, and confirmation that all UI actions (not just run/project management) are API-accessible.
